name: export
description: The ways to take something away as a file: a line saying what, and a link for each format that fits it, each naming the kind of file, its format and its size, downloaded with a plain link that needs no script.

use.when: a record, a list, a calendar or the whole workspace can be taken away as a file.
use.not: a link to a file someone added, which opens it (see the record's own page), or an action that changes something.
use.with: what is in the files said once, such as these 12 tasks, and only the formats that fit it.

what.description: What the files hold, after Download: this task, these 12 tasks, everything in Home. Said once in sight, and at the end of each link's name so a link read on its own still says what it downloads.

items.description: One link per format, most useful first.

href.description: Where the file is: a plain GET that answers with Content-Disposition: attachment.

format.description: The kind of file, which names the link: csv Spreadsheet (CSV), xlsx Excel (XLSX), vcf Contacts (vCard), ics Calendar (ICS), md Text (Markdown), html Web page (HTML), docx Word (DOCX), pdf Printable (PDF), zip Everything (ZIP), srt Subtitles (SRT), txt Plain text (TXT).

size.description: How big the file is, such as 4 KB or about 12 MB, when it is cheap to know. Leave out rather than guess.

note.description: One sentence under the links, only when what is in the files is not plain from what, such as what everything holds and what it leaves out.

id.description: Names the line that says what, so the list of links is named by it. Give one when two are on a page.

a11y.role: a paragraph naming a list of links; each link downloads a file

keyboard.does: downloads that file; the page stays where it is

wcag.notes: Each link's visible words say the kind of file, its format and its size (GOV.UK, NN/g), and its name ends with what it holds, so it makes sense read on its own (2.4.9) and starts with what is seen (2.5.3). The list is named by the line above it (1.3.1). Links look like quiet buttons, underlined, 44px high (2.5.5). A download changes nothing on the page and starts only when pressed (3.2.5).

machine.identify: Each a[download] is one file; data-format says which (csv, xlsx, vcf, ics, md, html, docx, pdf, zip, srt, txt) and href is where it is.
machine.operate: GET the href. The answer is the file, with Content-Type and a Content-Disposition filename; nothing on the page changes.

props.note: Every record as Markdown, every file as it was added, and a spreadsheet of each kind of record. Conversations and the log stay here.
